    2. Include an abstract section
    3. Include an introduction section

    To find papers to cite, use the available tools to search for papers by title. You must cite at least 3 papers from the list above. For each paper you cite, you must include its arXiv ID and title in the citation.
    
    The evaluation will check if your paper properly cites at least 3 papers from the list above by verifying the arXiv IDs match the paper titles.

execute_command(command="cat > /app/paper.txt << 'EOF'
Research Advances in Code Agents and Red-teaming

Abstract
========

The rapid advancement of code-generating artificial intelligence agents has revolutionized software development, enabling automated code generation, debugging, and execution. However, these powerful code agents introduce novel security vulnerabilities and trustworthiness concerns that require systematic evaluation. In this paper, we survey the latest research advances in code agents and red-teaming methodologies for assessing their safety and reliability. We examine how red-teaming techniques can be applied to identify vulnerabilities, biases, and unsafe behaviors in code agents. We analyze existing red-teaming frameworks, including RedCodeAgent, which provides automatic red-teaming capabilities against diverse code agents. Furthermore, we discuss the broader context of trustworthiness evaluation in AI systems, drawing on comprehensive assessments of GPT models. Finally, we explore the foundational deep learning architectures that enable these code generation capabilities, including residual learning approaches. Our survey highlights key challenges and identifies promising directions for future research in secure and trustworthy code agent development.

Introduction
============

Code agents represent a paradigm shift in how artificial intelligence systems interact with programming and software development. Unlike traditional code completion tools, modern code agents possess the ability to understand complex requirements, generate multi-file codebases, execute code iteratively, and debug their own outputs. These capabilities have been dramatically enhanced by the integration of large language models (LLMs) with code interpreters and development environments.

While the capabilities of code agents have advanced rapidly, significant concerns remain regarding their safety, security, and reliability. Code agents may inadvertently generate malicious code, expose sensitive information, introduce security vulnerabilities, or behave unpredictably in edge cases. The autonomous nature of these agents—capable of executing code and modifying systems—amplifies the potential impact of such failures.

Red-teaming, the practice of systematically probing AI systems for vulnerabilities and unsafe behaviors, has emerged as a critical methodology for ensuring the trustworthiness of AI systems. Traditionally applied to large language models for detecting harmful content generation, red-teaming is now being adapted for the unique challenges posed by code agents. Code-specific red-teaming must address not only text-based safety concerns but also the execution of potentially harmful code, security vulnerabilities in generated software, and the reliable operation of autonomous agents.

This paper provides a comprehensive survey of research advances at the intersection of code agents and red-teaming. We examine the landscape of code agent architectures, review existing red-teaming methodologies, and analyze frameworks specifically designed for code agent evaluation. We also contextualize these developments within the broader field of AI trustworthiness assessment.

Related Work
============

The field of code agent red-teaming has seen rapid development, with several key works establishing foundational frameworks and methodologies. RedCodeAgent: Automatic Red-teaming Agent against Diverse Code Agents (arXiv:2510.02609) introduces an automated framework for conducting red-teaming assessments against various code agent architectures. This work addresses the unique challenge of testing code agents by generating targeted adversarial prompts designed to elicit unsafe behaviors, such as the generation of malicious code, exploitation of security vulnerabilities, or unauthorized system access. The RedCodeAgent framework systematically evaluates code agents across multiple dimensions including code safety, security vulnerability generation, and adherence to ethical guidelines. By automating the red-teaming process, this approach enables scalable and reproducible evaluation of code agent safety.

The broader context of trustworthiness evaluation for generative AI models provides essential methodological foundations for code agent assessment. DecodingTrust: A Comprehensive Assessment of Trustworthiness in GPT Models (arXiv:2306.11698) presents an extensive evaluation framework for assessing multiple dimensions of trustworthiness in generative language models. This work establishes comprehensive benchmarks for measuring safety, bias, factual accuracy, and robustness across various GPT model variants. The methodologies developed in DecodingTrust, including adversarial testing procedures and systematic evaluation protocols, have been adapted for code-specific trustworthiness assessments. The framework's approach to multi-dimensional evaluation is particularly relevant for code agents, which must be assessed not only for the safety of generated text but also for the security implications of executable code outputs.

The underlying deep learning architectures that power modern code agents have been built upon foundational advances in neural network design. Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition (arXiv:1512.03385) introduced the residual learning framework that revolutionized deep neural network training by enabling the construction of substantially deeper architectures. This work established the residual block architecture and skip connections that have become standard components in modern transformer models, including those powering code generation systems. The ability to train networks with 100+ layers, as demonstrated in this foundational work, directly enabled the development of the large-scale transformer models that form the basis of contemporary code agents.

Recent work has extended these methodological foundations to address code-specific challenges. The combination of automated red-teaming frameworks, comprehensive trustworthiness evaluation methodologies, and advanced neural architectures has created a robust toolkit for assessing and improving code agent safety. However, significant challenges remain in developing standardized evaluation protocols, understanding the full scope of potential failure modes, and creating effective mitigation strategies for identified vulnerabilities.

Conclusion
==========

The field of code agents represents a rapidly evolving area of AI research with significant implications for software development practices and security. As code agents become more capable and widely deployed, the need for systematic safety evaluation through red-teaming becomes increasingly critical. This survey has highlighted key research advances, including automated red-teaming frameworks like RedCodeAgent, comprehensive trustworthiness assessment methodologies from the DecodingTrust work, and the foundational neural architecture innovations from the Deep Residual Learning research.

Several key observations emerge from our review. First, code agent red-teaming requires methodologies that extend beyond traditional language model safety assessment to address the unique risks of executable code generation. Second, comprehensive evaluation frameworks must account for multiple dimensions of trustworthiness, from code safety to security vulnerabilities to ethical considerations. Third, the underlying deep learning architectures continue to evolve, necessitating ongoing reassessment of agent capabilities and limitations.

Future research directions include the development of standardized benchmarks for code agent evaluation, the creation of more sophisticated automated red-teaming techniques that can uncover novel vulnerability classes, and the integration of safety considerations directly into code agent training and deployment pipelines. Additionally, research into formal verification methods for generated code and the development of defensive programming practices for agents operating in untrusted environments represent promising avenues for enhancing the trustworthiness of code agent systems.

As the field continues to advance, collaboration between researchers in code generation, security, and AI safety will be essential for ensuring that code agents develop responsibly and can be deployed with appropriate safeguards. The methodologies and frameworks surveyed in this paper provide a foundation for ongoing research and development in this critical area.

References
==========

[1] Chengquan Guo, Chulin Xie, Yu Yang, et al. "RedCodeAgent: Automatic Red-teaming Agent against Diverse Code Agents." arXiv:2510.02609, 2025.

[2] Boxin Wang, Weixin Chen, Hengzhi Pei, et al. "DecodingTrust: A Comprehensive Assessment of Trustworthiness in GPT Models." arXiv:2306.11698, 2023.

[3] Kaiming He, Xiangyu Zhang, Shaoqing Ren, Jian Sun. "Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition." arXiv:1512.03385, 2015.
EOF")
